 Authorities having jurisdiction (AHJs) enforce the NEC through enacted laws and regulations at the state or local level. Electrical inspectors are essentially the last line of defense in electrical safety for building owners and occupants by ensuring NEC-compliant installations. It is critical that required permits be attained, and all necessary inspections take place, in order to ensure that electrical inspectors be part of establishing safe installations.

[web-nfpa-org-learn-more-about-nfpa-70-national-electrical-cod.md] (dated 2026) A Brief History of the Early NEC
 In the late 1800s, the world was rapidly becoming more electrified. As a result, a fragmented collection of multiple safety standards addressing electrical installations were issued. Seeking to create a single, collective electrical standard, a meeting was held in New York City in March 1896, and a group called the Joint Conference of Electrical and Allied Interests was formed. This alliance consisted of various insurance, electrical, architectural, and other groups with a shared goal of keeping people and property safe from electrical hazards. This group would later go on to create and publish the first edition of the National Electrical Code in 1897. At that time, the document was also designated as National Board of Fire Underwriters Pamphlet 70 (NBFU 70) , which is the first association of the NEC with the number 70.

[web-nfpa-org-learn-more-about-nfpa-70-national-electrical-cod.md] (dated 2026) In some capacity, the NEC is utilized and enforced  in all 50 states in the U.S. It should be noted that, often based on the local legislative process, many states may enforce editions of the NEC that are not the most current. In some cases, municipalities within states will incorporate an edition of the NEC by reference into their locally amended  electrical code, such as in the case of Chicago and New York City. In these cases, it is possible that the local city authorities may be enforcing an entirely different edition of the NEC than the rest of the state; therefore, it is important to check with local jurisdictions as to which edition of the NEC is being enforced in the area.

[web-nfpa-org-learn-more-about-nfpa-70-national-electrical-cod.md] (dated 2026) The NEC is available for purchase in both print and digital formats. For professionals who need more robust tools and flexible access, NFPA LiNK ®  provides digital access to current and previous editions of the NEC, including some Spanish-language editions, powerful search and navigation capabilities, and other features. Whether you're working in the field, the classroom, or the office, NFPA LiNK is a comprehensive digital tool that helps you work faster, smarter, and safer.
